The packet contains no caller, no permission or role data, no traces, no proxy/init events and no oracle or price inputs, so no exploit mechanism can be named.
ai.lossBearer: Unidentified: the holder of record at 0x3c5d22fa3d916f8414141f4a277f59159091f366. No protocol, token-holder class or integrator exposure is shown in the packet.
ai.narrative: A single Ethereum transaction emptied one address of its whole USDC balance: 13,001,509.226442 USDC, roughly $13,001,509, with drained exposure recorded at $12,998,457. That is the entire story the packet tells. There is nothing here about who signed it, whether the mover held a legitimate admin or owner role, or what kind of contract this is. A full-balance sweep looks identical whether it is a hack, a treasury consolidation, a bridge settlement or a contract migration. Integrator exposure is an empty list, so no downstream victim is demonstrated either. Without a mechanism and without a named loss bearer, there is no supportable loss path to trade against.
